races.name: TRM Ironxcell For Energy Race

runners_data.name: Tolebi
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist trained by Gerard O'Leary, only four days since last run, but recent form string shows a string of mid-field finishes with no win from 11 starts; the step back to six furlongs from seven is slight help yet it needs a strong pace to close into — one this race may not provide.

runners_data.name: Michael's Well
runners_data.note: Eddie & Patrick Harty's three-year-old returns after 86 days off and is a true hold-up horse that the race map places in midfield purely because there is no room at the rear in this field configuration — racing outside its natural position materially reduces its chance in a slow-motion pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Likedbymike
runners_data.note: Four-year-old hold-up type with five places from 15 starts on similar Going; J M Sheridan rides off a mark of 94 which is competitive, but the horse's tendency to finish fifth-to-tenth in big fields and lack of a win since lowering its grade suggests it needs everything to fall right.

runners_data.name: Port Arthur
runners_data.note: W J Lee takes the ride on M C Grassick's lightly-raced three-year-old returning after 291 days off an OR of 120 — by far the highest-rated runner in the field — but that rating and only two career starts make fitness the key question; a prominent run to confirm a return to form is the likely outcome.

runners_data.name: Bear On The Run
runners_data.note: Shane Foley partners Daniel Murphy's three-year-old on its first outing in 353 days; showed genuine front-running ability when winning at Slane and holds the single most important tactical asset in this race — a clear lead with nothing willing to chase.

runners_data.name: Focaccia
runners_data.note: J A Stack's three-year-old is a prominent racer with one win from eight starts, all on Good ground at five and six furlongs; Gavin Ryan rides and the horse should settle just off the pace, but recent form (including an eighth last time at this trip on identical Going) tempers confidence.

races.paceDynamic: Bear On The Run is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with only one horse wired to lead in a six-runner field, shapes to dictate from the gates at a measured, uncontested gallop on Good turf at Naas over six furlongs. Port Arthur and Focaccia are the prominent types who will look to sit just off that pace, meaning the early complexion is orderly rather than pressured, which strongly favours Bear On The Run's ability to control tempo and steal a march from the front. The field contains more hold-up types than can genuinely operate from the rear — Michael's Well has been redistributed to midfield on the map but is a true hold-up horse racing out of its natural role, which compromises its chance in a shape where the tempo is unlikely to be fast enough to reel in a front-runner. This race shape most favours prominent-to-lead profiles: a controlled, honest gallop on Good ground with a single pace-setter will reward those racing on or near the speed rather than those waiting for a strong pace to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bear On The Run Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Bear On The Run breaks cleanly and dictates an honest but uncontested gallop, grinding rivals into submission.
scenarios.body: Bear On The Run sets a sustainable pace from the front with no challenger to force the tempo higher, leaving those in behind with no strong gallop to close into. Shane Foley's positional intelligence on a horse returning after 353 days that showed course-winning ability on similar Good ground makes this the dominant shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Bear On The Run's long absence blunts its early pace and Port Arthur or Focaccia are able to press hard and hit the front inside the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Bear On The Run's 353-day absence is a genuine vulnerability, and if that fitness deficit shows through the final furlong the prominent pair are ideally positioned to pounce. Port Arthur's OR of 120 carries significant class for this grade and W J Lee would be poised to exploit any fade.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closer Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If Bear On The Run sets a genuinely strong pace that collapses late and Likedbymike or Tolebi find room to close.
scenarios.body: Likedbymike has shown repeat place form at five and six furlongs on Good ground and could be the beneficiary if the front-runners burn each other up, though its OR of 94 and wide-draw history present hurdles. Tolebi operates from hold-up but recent form reads poorly and this scenario relies on a pace collapse that a lone front-runner is unlikely to engineer.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Michael's Well Surprises
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected, forcing genuine pressure, and Michael's Well — despite racing out of its natural hold-up role — produces a finishing burst from mid-division.
scenarios.body: Michael's Well is a genuine hold-up horse mapped to midfield and racing out of role, meaning this scenario depends on untypical race positioning and a pace scenario that current evidence does not support. The [STYLE_FIT=0.92] tag and 86-day absence compound the risk, making this the lowest-probability shape.

watchPoints.text: Bear On The Run — watch the break from the gates; if Shane Foley secures the lead uncontested, the race is his to control and the rest of the field faces a significant tactical problem at this pace scenario.
Port Arthur — 291 days off for a lightly-raced three-year-old means fitness is genuinely unverified; if it loses its position entering the final two furlongs, its class advantage is wasted.

Michael's Well — confirm it is settling in mid-division rather than its natural rear position; if forced to race even further back than mapped, its 86-day absence and style mismatch make it virtually impossible to win from off a slow pace.

Tolebi — only four days since last run; monitor whether that quick turnaround affects its early energy, as a hold-up horse in a race with a single front-runner needs to be at peak sharpness to make late ground count.

Focaccia — watch the opening two furlongs for whether Gavin Ryan commits to tracking Bear On The Run closely; if it concedes ground early and drops to midfield, its chance of winning diminishes sharply.

races.name: Matchbook Betting Exchange Handicap

runners_data.name: Amiata
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist trained by G M Lyons, ridden by Colin Keane — form figure of 1 last time out over 5f on Good is encouraging, and a step up to 6f on same going suits; 61-day absence is the main query but the stable runs horses fresh with success|

runners_data.name: Red Evolution
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Dylan Browne McMonagle who has found 5f on the sharp side and this 6f trip on Good ground matches his two best efforts including a win on this going; no headgear but the tongue-tie is a known factor and a return to 6f looks the key angle|

runners_data.name: Gavoo
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a strong 2W at 6f on Good ground in his last two visits to this trip; David Marnane's visor-wearer ran 5th here most recently at this distance, and at 137lbs the weight is not trivial, but the course-and-distance profile is live|

runners_data.name: Moltophino
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer who runs routinely on Good ground (13 of 15 runs at similar going) but has not troubled the judge recently — the 20th on his form string is a concern and the tongue-tie/pads combination has not unlocked improvement despite regular use|

runners_data.name: Spodo Komodo
runners_data.note: Front-runner for Ronan Whelan who won over 6f on Soft and has placed twice at similar going; quick 12-day turnaround following a flat effort and stepping back to 6f from 7f is a positive, and he is the most likely pace-setter to get first run if rivals fight amongst themselves early|

runners_data.name: Smoke Them Out
runners_data.note: Another confirmed front-runner, apprentice Sadhbh Tormey takes a 7lb claim which partially offsets the pace role; has form over 5f-7f on Good but the recent record away from his best trips is mixed, and as the lowest-rated pace-setter (OR 76) he is most at risk when the tempo bites|

runners_data.name: Leveraging
runners_data.note: Front-runner explicitly tagged as a fader in the finish — the last-time-out 0 at OR 79 and form figures of 9-6-10 on Good ground are discouraging; Robbie Colgan takes the ride but this horse looks likely to set the pace and then be passed, rather than convert it|

runners_data.name: Clonmacash
runners_data.note: Declan McDonogh rides this prominent type for Adrian McGuinness who has two winners in 24 days; visor-wearing 5-year-old has placed twice at 6f on Good in the last five starts and the consistency figures (5th, 3rd, 4th, 5th, 3rd) suggest a recurring placed-horse profile rather than a winning one|

runners_data.name: Gotta Catch'em All
runners_data.note: In-form hold-up horse (11 on last two starts) for H Rogers, placed to midfield on the map because the true rear is overcrowded — this horse will likely race further back than the map suggests; the blinkers are a known headgear angle and the Good-ground course wins are the standout angle, but racing out of natural position tempers confidence|

runners_data.name: Flaming Rib
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up type for McGuinness who is mapped to midfield despite preferring to race from off the pace — the visor is worn again and the recent 8th at 6f on Good reflects the difficulty of getting a clear run when shuffled back; no wins at this going in recent history and the style mismatch makes this a tough ask|

runners_data.name: Lohoobb
runners_data.note: Prominent-to-midfield type for W J Lee who has placed twice at 6f on Good and is unbeaten course record in similar conditions (7/7 at this going); 41-day absence is manageable, and the consistent placed form suggests this horse finds a way into proceedings without threatening the top|

races.paceDynamic: Leveraging, Spodo Komodo, and Smoke Them Out are all confirmed front-runners over this 6f Naas trip on Good ground, making a strong, contested gallop from the outset virtually inevitable — none of these three will yield willingly and the early fractions will be brisk. Smoke Them Out (apprentice claim, OR 76) and Spodo Komodo (OR 78, quick turnaround) will push Leveraging (OR 79, tagged as a fader) hard from the gates, meaning the pace-setters are likely to burn each other out before the two-furlong pole. This sets up a race where the leaders string the field out and leave themselves vulnerable in the closing stages, creating a genuine stamina test even over 6f. The pace shape strongly favours horses who can travel just off the boil in a prominent or mid-division berth and pick up the pieces as the pace-setters capitulate — note that Gotta Catch'em All and Flaming Rib are genuine hold-up types reassigned to midfield on the map because the rear of the field is already crowded; of the front-running trio, Spodo Komodo appears best-equipped on form to survive the tempo it helps create, but the profile that benefits most is the fresh, well-handicapped prominent racer who tracks the pace without fighting for it.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners burn each other out inside the final 2f, leaving the back-straight pace unsustainable
scenarios.body: The heated early gallop set by Leveraging, Spodo Komodo, and Smoke Them Out ensures the closing stages become a stamina test, with the leaders stopping in front of horses tracking just behind; horses who travel smoothly in midfield and hold a natural closing gear are rewarded as the winner comes from off the pace

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent-position horse travels comfortably behind the speed and produces a well-timed challenge from 2f out
scenarios.body: With the pace honest and the leaders racing competitively against each other, a horse sitting second or third without over-exerting conserves enough energy to reel in the tiring front pair; Red Evolution and Clonmacash both have the tactical versatility to occupy this ground if they jump cleanly

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is slightly less frenetic than expected and one of the three leads can settle into a rhythm and nick a lead into the straight
scenarios.body: Spodo Komodo, the most recent winner among the pace trio and carrying the least weight alongside Smoke Them Out, is the most likely candidate to convert front-running into a result if the others take each other on and allow a slight easing of tempo; this scenario is conditional on either Leveraging or Smoke Them Out failing to sustain early pressure

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Finishers Land Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the pace truly collapses and horses from the rear of the field generate enough momentum to reach the leaders in the final furlong
scenarios.body: Gotta Catch'em All is a genuine hold-up type reassigned to midfield on the map and will likely race further back than shown; if the fractions are truly severe and the closers find a clear run, a late burst is possible, but the redistribution of true hold-up horses means this scenario depends on horses racing out of their natural position and is therefore discounted

watchPoints.text: Leveraging is an explicit pace-setter with a fade flag — watch whether Ronan Colgan attempts to restrain him early to conserve energy, which could alter the entire shape of the race if one of the three front-runners drops away before the turn

Gotta Catch'em All and Flaming Rib are genuine hold-up horses mapped to midfield — watch their starting positions and early berths, as if they are unable to secure a natural position they will need an unusually strong pace collapse to get competitive

Smoke Them Out carries an apprentice with a 7lb claim (Sadhbh Tormey) and may be ridden more conservatively than expected — if she elects to track rather than lead, the pace dynamic softens materially and a prominent-tracker scenario becomes more likely

Red Evolution's best form has come at 5f on Good; this 6f trip is a slightly new test and Dylan Browne McMonagle will likely seek to position handily early to avoid being left behind if the fractions are fast — his positioning in the first furlong is worth monitoring

Amiata returns after 61 days for G M Lyons, a yard that fires horses fit fresh — Colin Keane's decision on how far back to drop in a fast-run race will determine whether the hold-up profile is an asset or a liability today

races.name: Matchbook Supporting Local Racing Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Caffu Zafeen
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with poor recent form (three sixes and two zeros), jockey Reese Holohan takes a 4lb claim but the 46-day break and a 0-from-7 record on sim going make this an uphill task from the rear.|

runners_data.name: Tawaazon
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up type with a genuinely useful 1W3P record on good and sim-going across 13 runs; tongue-tie fitted, returns after just 16 days and the second-best sim-going record in the field for hold-up horses is a tangible asset.|

runners_data.name: Reinforce
runners_data.note: Needs to come from off the pace but has faded in the finish repeatedly and the 0-from-12 record on good going is a serious concern; Robyn Donaghue-Leahy's 4lb claim is the main positive on a horse that looks to be in a tough spot tactically.|

runners_data.name: Dandy Land
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who will likely set an uncontested lead; visored for concentration, recent Naas run shows form at the trip and 5-from-7 on sim going is solid, though trainer W McCreery is 0 wins from 11 in the past 14 days which is worth noting.|

runners_data.name: Hot To Foxtrot
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type by nature, pushed into a midfield slot on the map because the field is saturated with rear-runners; the horse carries a STYLE_FIT flag and its best form has come when getting its true position — four places from six on good-ground 5f suggests ability, but the overcrowded hold-up group will make life difficult.|

runners_data.name: Practical Move
runners_data.note: Hold-up three-year-old who placed fourth at this trip on good going most recently; Julian Pietropaolo takes a 4lb claim and the horse drops to a light 135lbs, sitting in a more realistic midfield berth rather than deep rear.|

runners_data.name: Undefeatable
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on good ground earlier in the career but has been held up in a field where true hold-up ground is scarce; blinkers fitted, the STYLE_FIT tag tempers expectations and a 10th-place last run at 6f on good is not encouraging.|

runners_data.name: Another Nice'day
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading in the finish and tagged as a redistributed hold-up type; the 3-year-old showed a win at 5f on good but the recent run of 14th and 13th at 6f and 7f suggests she wants conditions to fall perfectly, and the overcrowded rear group makes that unlikely today.|

runners_data.name: Platino Bianco
runners_data.note: Recent winner at 5f on good ground and ran five times at the course at 5f and 6f on good; dropped to a 10-day turnaround and the prominent style genuinely fits this race shape, making it one of the better-positioned horses in the field.|

runners_data.name: Star Allure
runners_data.note: Returning from 92 days off and has only 3 runs on good or similar going from 15 attempts with zero wins or places on sim going; the redistribution into midfield from a natural hold-up position adds further risk to a horse that needs everything to go right.|

runners_data.name: Step Back In Time
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old prominent type with a 3W4P record at the course over 5f and 6f on good; Nicola Burns claims 2lbs and the profile genuinely suits tracking the leader, though recent form shows a sequence of 9th, 14th and 12th and the flat trajectory is a concern.|

runners_data.name: Steel Magnolia
runners_data.note: Consistent placer at 5f on good-ish surfaces with four placings from recent runs; held up naturally but mapped to midfield due to overcrowding, the STYLE_FIT flag applies and the visor is retained — the 31-day break is neutral.|

runners_data.name: Luminessa
runners_data.note: Hold-up three-year-old with two runs on good going placing 10th and 7th, so limited evidence of getting competitive on this surface; the 52-day layoff adds uncertainty and the tongue-tie and hood combo suggests the yard is trying to find the right gear.|

runners_data.name: Jackandthefox
runners_data.note: Prominent-style seven-year-old who has placed four and five at 6f and 7f on good going in recent starts; no claim for Wesley Joyce and the drop to 5f is a slight query, but the natural front-of-field style is well matched to this race shape.|

runners_data.name: Livingston Range
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up type redistributed into midfield on the map; has placed 4th and 4th twice at 6f on good going but the STYLE_FIT flag, trainer 0-from-5 run, and the crowded hold-up group all limit the realistic upside here.|

races.paceDynamic: Dandy Land is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 15-runner field and, with no genuine rival expected to press hard from the gates, will control the fractions through the first half of this 5f on good turf at Naas. Platino Bianco and Step Back In Time are the primary prominent challengers who will track Dandy Land but are unlikely to force a truly contested gallop, meaning the pace is set to be sustainable rather than scorching. The field holds more hold-up and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate — Hot To Foxtrot, Another Nice'day, Undefeatable, Luminessa, Steel Magnolia and Livingston Range are all true hold-up horses redistributed toward midfield on the map, with Platino Bianco and Step Back In Time most likely to actually secure prominent ground behind Dandy Land. A solo front-runner controlling a steady-to-fair pace on flat good ground at 5f classically suits horses who can travel prominently and sustain their effort through the final furlong — prominent trackers and horses with a reliable finishing kick from the second rank are most favoured here, while genuine hold-up horses face the additional burden of covering ground from further back than ideal.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dandy Land Controls, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Dandy Land dictates an uncontested lead and prominent trackers sustain through the final furlong
scenarios.body: Dandy Land sets the fractions alone and the pace is fair but not suicidal, allowing horses racing just off the shoulder to conserve energy and quicken in the closing stages; Platino Bianco, with a recent win over this exact C&D configuration and strong going form, is ideally placed to pounce, while Step Back In Time can maximise its prominent style.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Holds, Front Runner Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the pace remains genuinely steady and Dandy Land's fitness edge carries it to the line from the front
scenarios.body: With only modest pressure from rivals, Dandy Land is never asked a serious question until the final 100 yards and the horse's recent proximity in a similar scenario suggests it can sustain the effort; the visor may sharpen its concentration and a lightly-challenged leader on good ground over 5f is a live winning profile.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is quicker than anticipated and a hold-up horse catches a collapsing field in the final strides
scenarios.body: Should the prominent battle between Dandy Land, Platino Bianco and Step Back In Time produce a faster early sectional, the field may string out and leave a clear passage for a well-placed midfield horse to deliver a late run; Tawaazon has the best recent sim-going record in the hold-up group and Practical Move showed a fourth at this trip on good ground, giving both a realistic profile if gaps appear.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Outsider Capitalises
scenarios.trigger: If the field fans wide, traffic is poor in the held-up group and an overlooked prominent type finds a clear passage
scenarios.body: In a 15-runner sprint on good ground, positional chaos can disadvantage even well-fancied hold-up horses and elevate a lesser-fancied prominent type who avoids the squeeze; Jackandthefox has consistent placed form at 6f on good ground and can travel up with the pace, making it the most likely beneficiary of a messy race.

watchPoints.text: Platino Bianco — a recent 5f winner at Naas on good going returns in just 10 days and is the prominent horse best placed to capitalise if Dandy Land controls the fractions at a fair pace; watch for a smooth move to Dandy Land's shoulder at the 2f pole.

Dandy Land — confirmed lone front-runner under a visor; if allowed to bowl along unchallenged at a controlled pace on flat good ground, the horse becomes dangerous as a potential hold-on winner rather than just a pacemaker.

Hot To Foxtrot and Undefeatable — both are genuine hold-up horses pushed further forward than their natural position by the overcrowded rear group; watch for them to be caught in traffic or forced to use energy earlier than ideal, which would compromise their finishing effort.

Another Nice'day — flagged for fading in the finish and holds a STYLE_FIT note; if the pace stays fair and the hold-up group is compressed behind, this runner is at risk of being pocketed and unable to produce its natural closing run.

Step Back In Time — prominent style suits but recent form is poor; watch whether Nicola Burns can position this horse in the slipstream of Dandy Land early, as finding that rail berth in a 15-runner field could be the difference between a placing and another mid-field effort.

races.name: Bet 20 Get 40 With Matchbook Handicap

runners_data.name: Altimara
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who handles Good going well (9 from 15 sim-going entries, 2 wins) but all recent form has come over 7f-8f and she steps back to 7f here; Ross O'Sullivan yard has been quiet and she needs a truly run race to get competitive from off the pace at OR 70.

runners_data.name: Lough Leane
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type who has won over a mile-plus and most of her form comes over longer distances — this 7f trip may not see her at her best; the 7lb claimer Jessica O'Gorman rides, and 42 days since last run needs to be considered alongside a yard showing 1 from 3 in the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Chester Nimitz
runners_data.note: Travels in headgear (hood and tongue-tie) and won over 6f on Good ground, making the step up to 7f a question; Gary Carroll is a strong booking but the horse's recent form includes several non-placed efforts and the OR of 67 leaves little room.

runners_data.name: Rappell
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on Good at Naas recently and placed at 7f on the same surface — Dylan Browne McMonagle is the standout jockey booking here; runs from hold-up position but has shown the ability to quicken effectively, with ten runs on similar going from fifteen attempts underlining suitability for today's conditions.

runners_data.name: Phoenix Pairc
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse by nature whose one win came over 7f at Staplestown and who has placed at this trip before, but the congested hold-up group means it is unlikely to get its natural position at the rear; the STYLE_FIT tag (0.92) reflects the squeeze, and W J Lee will need a clean run that may not materialise in a 19-runner field.

runners_data.name: Dynamic Force
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner here, with a 7-year-old who won and placed at 7f on Good going and has raced fourteen times on similar ground — the pace map pivots entirely around his willingness to roll; Sadhbh Tormey (7lb claimer) takes the ride, which is the one slight query on whether the tempo is managed optimally, but the horse's strong sim-going record (14/15) is a major positive.

runners_data.name: Mo Anam Chara
runners_data.note: 3-year-old who won over 8f on Good ground at last start and placed over 8f on Fibresand, but only one run from six on today's going type; the step down to 7f is untested and 77 days off the track for Mark Fahey's yard introduces a significant unknown, though the form figures at face value are respectable.

runners_data.name: Darkdeserthighway
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old veteran carrying a hood who is a genuine deep hold-up horse by habit, but the overflow of hold-up types forces him into the midfield pack rather than his natural position at the rear; M D O'Callaghan's runner has placed on soft-ish going over shorter trips and may find 7f on Good slightly sharp.

runners_data.name: Profit Surge
runners_data.note: Has posted multiple placed efforts at 5f-7f on Good ground (0W4P on sim-going from 6 runs) and is a consistent performer, yet his true hold-up style is compromised by redistribution into the midfield; Colin Keane is the best jockey in this field and his ability to thread through traffic is the main argument for keeping the horse in the reckoning.

runners_data.name: Sherekiya
runners_data.note: Unexposed 3-year-old trained by Dermot Weld who has been absent for 301 days — this is a significant flag; only one run on Good-type ground and a modest form line of 754 means she is one of the biggest unknowns in the field despite the trainer's reputation.

runners_data.name: Irish Rumour
runners_data.note: A consistent hold-up performer with 11 runs on Good going showing four places from 15 sim-going efforts, but the overflow of hold-up types means she is unlikely to get the clear passage she needs; Miss Jennifer Anne Lynch's runner has been placed at 6f on Good before but the 6-year-old appears to have a ceiling around her current OR of 61.

runners_data.name: Land Of The Giants
runners_data.note: One of only three genuine prominent types in the race and therefore tactically well-positioned if Dynamic Force sets a sensible gallop ahead of him; Adrian McGuinness has had two winners from 24 in the last fortnight and the horse's placed record over 7f-8f on Good going (3 places from 15 sim-going) suggests he handles the surface; the 10lb claimer Cillian Rowan is the query.

runners_data.name: Volendam
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on Good going and has placed twice at that trip on similar ground, but steps down to 7f where she is less exposed; one of only three prominent racers and therefore gets a prominent position naturally — J M Sheridan takes the ride for E D Delany, who has one winner from one in the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Bear Right
runners_data.note: A progressive 3-year-old for Mrs John Harrington (3 wins/31 runners recently) who wears a hood and whose form shows three consecutive third-place finishes; a genuine hold-up horse by inclination who is redistribued into midfield as a result of the congested hold-up pack, and the STYLE_FIT discount (0.92) is relevant though the trainer's form and Shane Foley's horsemanship keep him interesting.

runners_data.name: Zheleznaya Dama
runners_data.note: A 3-year-old prominent racer for Brendan Duke who has a fade-in-finish flag — has placed twice on Good going over 7f-8f but the concern about not lasting home is real over this trip; Rory Cleary's ability to conserve energy early will be key to whether the horse holds on.

runners_data.name: Frosted Sky
runners_data.note: A very lightly-raced 3-year-old (only three runs, all unplaced) whose form figures of 886 and fade-in-finish warning make this a very difficult race to assess; Daniel McLoughlin's runner has been off for 50 days and the redistribution from hold-up to midfield is a secondary issue behind the question of whether the horse is ready to compete in a 19-runner handicap.

runners_data.name: Summer Snow
runners_data.note: Top weight at OR 72 and the highest-rated horse in the field, but recent form of 0-9050 is deeply uninspiring; all turf form in similar going shows 8 from 15 entries, with three wins historically, yet the Peter Lawlor runner has no confirmed jockey listed which is an information gap, and the weight burden is the obvious hurdle.

runners_data.name: Suerte
runners_data.note: A 4-year-old hold-up type whose redistributed placement into midfield reflects the overcrowded hold-up contingent; form of 769-70 over 6f-8f on Good and Soft going shows she has yet to reach the frame and Ms Sheila Lavery's yard has no recent wins from five; the STYLE_FIT tag (0.90) flags that she is unlikely to operate from her natural position.

runners_data.name: Miss Ivor
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 3-year-old with only unplaced efforts, a fade-in-finish flag, and form over 12f, 8f and shorter in a consistent pattern of mid-to-back finishes; the absence of a confirmed jockey, 61 days since last run, and redistribution out of her natural hold-up berth combine to make this one of the most exposed at-risk runners in the race.

races.paceDynamic: Dynamic Force is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace pressure from another lead horse, is expected to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over this 7f trip on Good ground at Naas. Land Of The Giants and Volendam are the only other prominent types likely to track closely, meaning the pace is unlikely to be truly scorching — Dynamic Force can bowl along at a rhythm that suits a horse with stamina and tactical ease. This controlled tempo over 7f on a flat, fair track typically rewards horses who can sit just off the pace and pick up in the straight rather than deep closers who need a genuine searching gallop to produce their best. This field holds significantly more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Profit Surge, Bear Right, Phoenix Pairc, Darkdeserthighway, Irish Rumour, and Frosted Sky among others are genuine back-of-the-field horses who will be racing in a compressed, congested midfield rather than finding clear air late, which further tempers the case for pure hold-up horses. The tactical verdict is clear: a controlled pace with an uncontested front-runner and a congested hold-up group favours prominent-to-midfield horses who can travel smoothly in the slipstream and quicken from a good position in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dynamic Force Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Dynamic Force is allowed to roll along unchallenged and sets a steady-to-fair gallop that stretches the hold-up pack.
scenarios.body: Dynamic Force controls every yard, the pace is honest but not brutal, and horses racing close behind in the prominent-to-midfield berths get a perfect tow into the straight; the congested hold-up group are forced to navigate traffic and arrive too late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Hit The Line
scenarios.trigger: If Land Of The Giants or Volendam tracks Dynamic Force closely and the pace picks up two furlongs out, exposing the deep hold-up horses as too far back.
scenarios.body: The early-pace horses who sat handy quicken through the final furlong as the hold-up brigade get denied a clean run in a packed field; horses with good positional sense and strong recent form on Good ground thrive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace genuinely picks up early enough to string the field out and the hold-up horses get a clear run into the straight.
scenarios.body: A true end-to-end gallop would compress finishing margins and allow genuine hold-up horses to reel in a tiring leader; however this scenario is structurally discounted because several nominally late-running horses are redistributed from a congested midfield and may never find the clear passage they need.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Race Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If Dynamic Force is taken on or checks sharply and the race devolves into a slowly-run dash that becomes a sprint finish from the 2f pole.
scenarios.body: A messy, muddling race would suit a horse with raw speed who can quicken off a slow pace; however with 19 runners and multiple hold-up horses crammed into midfield, finding room in a bunched finish is extremely difficult.

watchPoints.text: Dynamic Force (front-runner, 7lb claimer Sadhbh Tormey) controls the entire pace map — if she allows the horse to drift or quickens early, every prominent and midfield horse's chance changes materially; watch the opening quarter mile closely.

Colin Keane on Profit Surge is a significant jockey-upgrade angle in a race where the congested hold-up group is the main structural problem — if he gets a clean run on the inner from midfield at the two-furlong pole, the horse's placed consistency could translate to a winning effort.

Bear Right (Shane Foley, Mrs John Harrington, three recent thirds) represents a trainer-jockey combination in strong form; the horse's redistribution out of its natural hold-up slot is a discount, but Foley's traffic-reading skill could overcome the positional squeeze.

Summer Snow carries the top weight of 142lbs with no confirmed jockey — any late booking, rider inexperience, or tactical error under that burden in a 19-runner race could derail a horse that has won three times on similar going and

races.name: Watch All Racing Live At Matchbook Handicap

runners_data.name: Daler
runners_data.note: Strong recent form — back-to-back placed efforts culminating in a Naas win over 9f on Soft, stepping up in trip now which looks a positive; hold-up style but has the tactical pace to track forward if needed and Gary Carroll is savvy enough to exploit a steady pace.

runners_data.name: Diamond Exchange
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner here and able to control the race from the front; one win and three places from seven starts at similar going suggests she handles Good well, and Shane Foley's booking for Harrington is a positive in a race she can dictate.

runners_data.name: Genoah
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse who wins off big trips (12f, Stanjames) but whose best chance here depends on getting a clear late run — held up behind a steady pace without a furious finish, the redistribution into midfield reflects real positional competition and STYLE_FIT of 0.93 tempers optimism.

runners_data.name: Nakasero
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead-trained hold-up type with a fair amount of slow-ground form; apprentice claim from Adam Grant is a mild positive but the horse has been beaten in similar fields and Good ground has produced mixed results — stay-on profile suits only if the pace truly quickens.

runners_data.name: Pavilion End
runners_data.note: Six-year-old veteran whose best recent result was a 2nd over 14f on Good — genuine hold-up runner now shuffled into midfield due to crowding at the rear; STYLE_FIT tag is a caution, and the horse's middle-distance limitations on straight handicap Naas trips are a concern.

runners_data.name: Letiza
runners_data.note: Trainer-ridden by Andrew Slattery which is unusual but the horse's recent 2nd on Good at 10f shows she retains ability; naturally held up, but the pace map puts her in a positional squeeze — the Good ground suits based on her 1W3P record, and she may benefit if the field fans out wide.

runners_data.name: Enchanted Lady
runners_data.note: Lightly raced four-year-old filly who hasn't run for 44 days, making this a notable absence; her form shows a 4th over 12f on Good which is the most relevant run, but she's held up by nature and hasn't yet proven she can win in this competitive environment — fitness on return is the key unknown.

runners_data.name: My Girl Grace
runners_data.note: Just two career runs but the most recent was a win over 10f on Soft for G M Lyons with Colin Keane retaining the ride — stepping up from that win into handicap company now, and the Keane-Lyons combination demands respect even if the form lines are thin; held up but young and lightly campaigned.

runners_data.name: Hamiyan
runners_data.note: Dermot Weld's three-year-old who has shown placed form up to 8f but now steps up sharply in trip to 1m2½f — natural hold-up type who will be racing in midfield among a crowded group; the trip rise is unproven and the STYLE_FIT of 0.90 is the weakest in the field, meaning positional compromise is most acute here.

runners_data.name: Big Dispute
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old with a well-worn handicap profile and a 690 recent form string that shows no win threat; redistributed into midfield from a natural rear position, the horse has multiple placings at 18-20f suggesting the shorter trip may be against him, and OR of 66 marks him as a weak entry at current ratings.

runners_data.name: Covert Legend
runners_data.note: Remarkably consistent placer — four 4th-place finishes in last five runs — but unable to win; six-year-old with form on Good going and a tendency to run into a place without ever truly threatening; held up by preference, now in midfield by necessity, and the headgear (tv) adds a small X-factor without changing the fundamental ceiling.

races.paceDynamic: Diamond Exchange is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner 1m2½f handicap and, with no genuine rival likely to press her hard from the outset on Good ground at Naas, she is set to control tempo from the front without meaningful pressure. The pace will therefore be honest but not brutal — a steadily-run gallop that suits a horse who can travel comfortably and produce a measured finish rather than a true staying test. The remainder of the field is dominated by hold-up horses, with Hamiyan, Genoah, Pavilion End, Letiza, and several others all natural come-from-behind types who will be competing for limited room at the rear and unable to all get their preferred positions, meaning several will race further forward than ideal. A lone, unhurried front-runner on Good turf over this trip creates a race shape that most rewards prominent or mid-division runners who can track the leader economically and pounce in the straight — pure hold-up closers face the added risk of a pace that never truly fully stretches out, leaving them with less to aim at late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Diamond Exchange Controls, Nearest Win
scenarios.trigger: If Diamond Exchange dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and the field strings out behind her at a steady pace.
scenarios.body: Diamond Exchange sets her own rhythm throughout, building a cushion that is never fully reeled in, while prominent trackers who travel fluidly into the straight gain an advantage over deep hold-up types who find insufficient late fractions to exploit.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If a horse travels in the top four throughout and produces a clean finishing effort when Diamond Exchange's lead is challenged turning in.
scenarios.body: The steady pace suits a horse like Daler or My Girl Grace who can lob just off the front and quicken into a gap in the straight without needing a strong end-to-end gallop to deliver.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Lucky Run
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sharply in the final two furlongs and gaps open for hold-up types to deliver late runs.
scenarios.body: A horse like Genoah or Letiza, forced wider into midfield, finds an unobstructed route and arrives with a late rattle — this depends on a pace lift that the lone front-runner scenario makes unlikely.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Overhauls Field
scenarios.trigger: If Diamond Exchange is left entirely alone and steals an unassailable lead through the final bend.
scenarios.body: Diamond Exchange, unchallenged and relaxed, simply extends her advantage in the straight and nothing from deep in the field has the pace reserves to close the gap on Good ground.

watchPoints.text: Diamond Exchange (front-runner) — if Shane Foley jumps cleanly and sets a genuinely unchallenged early tempo, the danger is that she simply steals enough of an advantage through the early stages that no hold-up horse can close the gap in the straight on Good ground.

Daler — watch whether Gary Carroll positions him prominently from the off rather than holding up; if Daler travels in the first three on the far rail turning in, his recent form makes him a live danger to the leader at the business end.

My Girl Grace — Colin Keane on a lightly-raced Lyons filly stepping up in trip; watch market moves before the off, as unexposed horses from this yard can be significantly better than their two-run profiles suggest.

Positional crowding at the rear — with at least seven horses carrying natural hold-up tendencies, watch for early jostling and shuffling back as riders compete for limited gap-finding positions in the straight; horses drawn widest may find it easier to secure a clear run.

Hamiyan — Chris Hayes stepping up Weld's three-year-old in trip from 8f to 1m2½f for the first time; if the horse is seen pulling early or refusing to settle, it signals the step up in distance is not working and the run can be safely dismissed.

races.name: Irish EBF Ballyhane Stakes (Median Sires Series)

runners_data.name: South Dakota
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for A P O'Brien with three runs on good ground and a best of third; Wayne Lordan keeps the faith but the consistent back-of-the-field positioning means he needs a genuinely run race to produce his late effort over just 6f.

runners_data.name: Star Prospect
runners_data.note: Lightly but actively raced 2yo for Joseph O'Brien with solid form at 5f including a win on soft; stepping up to 6f for the first time, Dylan Browne McMonagle's booking and a T14 of 15/80 makes this one of the yard's more fancied runners, and the prominent style suits this projected pace shape well.

runners_data.name: Eighteenth Smiles
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up type by inclination and recent race history, pushed into a midfield mapping here purely because the field has too many backmarkers to represent at the rear; Declan McDonogh will likely find himself further back than the map suggests, which dilutes the chance in a race unlikely to produce a strong enough pace to bring him into it.

runners_data.name: Ranting Duke
runners_data.note: Visored hold-up runner with a sole win (second at 6f on good) buried in modest form; the wide-margin defeat on debut and trainer's flat T14 of 0/3 do little to encourage, and a 30-day break adds further uncertainty from the back of the field.

runners_data.name: Starlit
runners_data.note: Complete unknown — no form lines, no going data, lightly raced flag from Mrs John Harrington; Shane Foley is an excellent booking and the trainer has a respectable T14 of 3/31, but without any evidence of style or ability this runner is a pure wildcard.

runners_data.name: Alpe d'Huez
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race and a course winner over today's trip; a 47-day break is worth noting, and his sole win came on standard ground rather than good, but Archie Watson's 2/19 T14 is workmanlike and the uncontested lead is a significant tactical asset.

runners_data.name: El Domino
runners_data.note: Trainer-ridden by Andrew Slattery, which is unusual and may signal a confidence issue or simple pragmatism; one run, a 6th on good, gives almost nothing to work with and the unknown style tag makes assigning a role in this race shape speculative at best.

runners_data.name: Anglesea Bridge
runners_data.note: Hold-up type from G M Lyons with two runs, both on good ground at 6f, finishing 14th and 5th — the form is improving but the closing position from the back looks insufficient unless the pace is honest; Robert Whearty takes the ride for a yard with a modest T14 of 2/17.

runners_data.name: Weekend Roar
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's only runner has a 1-2 record in two starts, both on good ground over 6f — course and distance form is the best in the race and the prominent style fits the projected shape perfectly; a 39-day gap is the only mild concern but W J Lee is a trusted pilot for the pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Lily Bear
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly whose two runs came at 8f and 7f on good and soft; stepping down to 6f makes her a pure speed question mark, the trainer sends out few runners (T14: 0/6), and a 7th and 10th on the board offer nothing to recommend her for this company.

runners_data.name: Livenka
runners_data.note: Colin Keane rides a filly in fine form — 3-3-1 on the board with all three runs on good ground including a 6f win; G M Lyons has a 2/17 T14 and Keane's presence is a strong positive, with the prominent style ideally matching what this race should produce tactically.

runners_data.name: Maeda Matsu
runners_data.note: Debut runner with no form lines and an unknown going tag; trainer Ms Sheila Lavery sends out very few runners (T14: 0/5) and Rory Cleary gets the ride, but without any evidence to work with this runner is impossible to place meaningfully in any scenario.

races.paceDynamic: Alpe d'Huez is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner 6f maiden and, with no genuine rival to pressure him from the gates, Gary Carroll should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop that never truly tests his stamina. Star Prospect, Weekend Roar, and Livenka are the prominent types most likely to sit just behind him in the first two or three, creating a relatively organised front group rather than a contested early burn. The true hold-up horses — South Dakota, Ranting Duke, Anglesea Bridge, and Lily Bear — will be covered up in the rear, facing a standard late challenge off a pace that may not be fast enough to stretch the field into a proper test for closers. This field holds more prominent and hold-up types than the map can naturally accommodate; of the redistributed and borderline runners, Star Prospect and Livenka are likeliest to actually secure their forward position, while Eighteenth Smiles, despite natural hold-up tendencies, is pushed into midfield by field size. The race shape decisively favours horses who can travel in behind a moderate leader and produce a sharp, sustained burst from two furlongs out — making prominent-to-midfield stalkers the profile to be on.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Alpe d'Huez Controls, Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Alpe d'Huez bowls along at a fair but uncontested pace and the prominent horses time their challenge to arrive in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Alpe d'Huez sets a comfortable tempo allowing Carroll to conserve petrol, while the well-positioned prominent horses — Livenka, Star Prospect, Weekend Roar — get an ideal tow into the race and unleash their finishing kick from two furlongs out; this shape rewards horses with a clean passage and the ability to quicken off a genuine but not frenetic pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Front Two Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Alpe d'Huez and one prominent rival steal a march and the midfield fails to close the gap in the straight.
scenarios.body: Carroll extends the lead turning for home and the hold-up horses, caught flat-footed at the back, find the distance too short to reel in the pace; horses who sat second or third — Star Prospect or Weekend Roar — inherit the slipstream and go with the leader rather than coming from behind.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Strong Pace, Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack pushes the tempo harder than expected and the early pace is fast enough to string the field out.
scenarios.body: A genuinely hot early gallop burns off the pace-setters' reserves, leaving the back-division horses — South Dakota, Livenka if eased back — with a collapsing target to run at; A P O'Brien's South Dakota, who has shown consistent form over this trip and going, is the likeliest beneficiary if the pace does honest work.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Unexposed Runner Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If one of the lightly raced or unknown-going runners — Starlit, Maeda Matsu, or El Domino — produces an on-debut or lightly-raced leap forward in class.
scenarios.body: A debutant or once-raced runner with unexposed ability capitalises on the clean run that a moderate pace affords, sitting midfield under a patient ride and cutting through tired horses in the final furlong; the lack of form lines makes these horses genuine unknowns, and a well-structured tactical race amplifies their upside.

watchPoints.text: Livenka and Weekend Roar both carry confirmed prominent styles, strong recent form on good ground over 6f, and top jockey bookings — watch whether they can both get their position behind Alpe d'Huez or whether one is forced to take back.

Alpe d'Huez has not run in 47 days and his sole win came on standard rather than good ground; if fitness or going sensitivity means he ties up in the final furlong, the race shape collapses and the whole tactical read changes.

Eighteenth Smiles is a genuine hold-up horse mapped to midfield purely by field congestion — watch whether Declan McDonogh elects to push forward against his horse's natural inclination or settles even further back than the map implies, which would significantly reduce its chance.

Star Prospect steps up from 5f to 6f for the first time today; if the extra furlong finds him out in the final stages despite a prominent position, Weekend Roar and Livenka are the immediate beneficiaries of that fading.

Three lightly raced or debut runners (Starlit, Maeda Matsu, El Domino) represent genuine pace unknowns — watch the early strides to see whether any break quickly and disrupt the assumed single-pace-setter narrative around Alpe d'Huez.

races.name: Hurling For Cancer On August 24th Fillies Maiden

runners_data.name: Dark Willow
runners_data.note: A six-year-old who races as a hold-up type, though she is mapped to midfield here as the field has too many rear-runners to place at the back; her form shows repeated fading in the closing stages and she has been off 257 days, making this a tough assignment.

runners_data.name: Zarenakarena
runners_data.note: Completely unexposed with no public form on record; the Eddie & Patrick Harty yard have one runner in the past 14 days, so watch market moves as the only guide to her readiness.

runners_data.name: Zesty Belle
runners_data.note: A hold-up filly returning from 248 days off with modest form on Tapeta at a mile-plus; the step onto Good turf and this competitive field makes improvement essential.

runners_data.name: Acula
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's debutante carries the best trainer strike rate in this field (15 winners from 80 in 14 days) and is bred to handle a mile on Good ground; market support would make her a serious contender purely on unknown potential.

runners_data.name: Emiza
runners_data.note: Dermot Weld's unraced three-year-old is lightly campaigned and the handler has strong form with first-time-out fillies at Naas; the Going is confirmed Good, which suits the Weld operation, and this represents an interesting unknown.

runners_data.name: Estrallita
runners_data.note: Jack Davison's first-time-out filly has a jockey booking (James Ryan) that is respectable, but the trainer's 0/2 in the past fortnight offers little statistical encouragement and she enters without any public evidence.

runners_data.name: Mardi Gras Queen
runners_data.note: Her sole run was a sixth over 7f on Heavy at Dundalk; she is a natural hold-up type squeezed forward on the pace map due to the volume of closers in this field, and dropping back to her true position will mean she needs the closers' scenario to materialise.

runners_data.name: My Girl Jersie
runners_data.note: Three runs all resulted in ninth on Heavy ground at The Curragh or Dundalk — the switch to Good turf is a significant change of conditions and the 280-day absence adds further uncertainty; her finishing tendency repeatedly fades, and the shape here does not help.

runners_data.name: Nautic Star
runners_data.note: The race's lone confirmed front-runner with recent competitive form at 7f-8f on Good, including two seconds; Shane Foley rides for Harrington who has 3/31 in 14 days, and Nautic Star's ability to control tempo without a rival is the defining factor in this race shape.

runners_data.name: Never The Same
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes the ride for Joseph O'Brien — a high-profile booking — on a filly who finished fourth over 7f Good last time; she is a genuine hold-up horse placed higher on the map because of overcrowding at the rear, so she ideally needs luck in running.

runners_data.name: Orellana
runners_data.note: An unraced three-year-old for Hamish Rogers with Siobhan Rutledge in the saddle; the yard has 2/6 in 14 days, modest but not without form, and without a racecourse marker her chance is entirely speculative.

runners_data.name: Shelton Spring
runners_data.note: Ran once six days ago and finished last of 12 over 7f on Good — the quick turnaround is notable, she fades in finishes, and as a natural hold-up type pushed up the map she is unlikely to improve significantly on that debut effort here.

runners_data.name: Sioux The Boss
runners_data.note: Ran last of 12 over 7f on Good 66 days ago; wears a hood (headgear flagged), is a genuine hold-up type redistributed forward, and fades in the closing stages — the race shape here with a single calm pace-setter does not favour her profile.

runners_data.name: Sweetie Too
runners_data.note: Ran tenth of 10 over 8f on Good 63 days ago; her finishing profile shows late fade and without any significant update from connections she represents an unexposed but unencouraging profile at this stage.

runners_data.name: Terra Di Siena
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's filly ran thirteenth over 10f on Good 52 days ago — stepping back in trip helps, but finishing last on her only start at a longer distance over Good ground is not the form required; she fades in finishes and the hold-up scenario this race demands is the least likely to materialise.

runners_data.name: Venosa
runners_data.note: Wayne Lordan rides for Aidan O'Brien — a notable booking — and the filly has the most experienced profile among the hold-up horses with six runs, including a third on Heavy at The Curragh; she is placed in midfield by redistribution, not by natural inclination, and Lordan's ability to place her tactically is her primary asset.

runners_data.name: Whatsin The Stars
runners_data.note: Ran eleventh over 8f on Good nine days ago wearing a hood; Paul Flynn has 3/20 in 14 days and the quick reappearance combined with a fading finish profile makes this a holding ticket unless the headgear sparks improvement.

runners_data.name: Xirivella
runners_data.note: Colin Keane rides for Noel Meade — a stable with 4/20 in 14 days — and the filly finished sixth over 8f on Good 30 days ago wearing a hood on debut; she is a hold-up type with one piece of experience under her belt and Keane's track intelligence at Naas gives her a tactical edge if she has improved.

races.paceDynamic: Nautic Star is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 18-runner fillies maiden and, with no other genuine pace horse to challenge her, Shane Foley can dictate terms at a controlled, sustainable gallop around Naas's flat mile. The pace will be modest from the outset — Nautic Star's recent form shows consistent prominence from the front and she will not be pressured into an unsustainable early tempo, meaning the race is likely to be run at a measured clip that keeps the field bunched through the early stages before quickening from the home turn. The field is heavily populated with hold-up types — Sioux The Boss, Shelton Spring, Never The Same, Mardi Gras Queen, Venosa, and others are genuine come-from-behind horses who have been mapped forward simply because the map cannot accommodate them all at the rear — with the result that several will race closer to the pace than their natural style dictates, compressing the midfield and reducing the advantage of any late finisher. This race shape — a single unhurried front-runner controlling a modest pace — strongly favours horses capable of travelling prominently or in the top half of the field and producing a sustained, measured finish, rather than those relying on a truly searching gallop to bring their late run into play.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Nautic Star Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Nautic Star leads at a calm tempo and the hold-up horses are denied a genuine test of stamina.
scenarios.body: Foley slots Nautic Star into an uncontested lead, sets a comfortable pace, and kicks at the two-furlong pole before the mass of closers can organise a coherent challenge; the modest gallop means the late runners are always chasing rather than reeling in a tiring leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just sufficient to stretch the field and a horse racing in the first half produces the best finishing effort.
scenarios.body: A horse sitting two or three lengths off Nautic Star through the middle stages tracks her every move and produces a clean, economical burst turning in, getting first run on the hold-up runners who are still threading through traffic.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Debutante/Lightly Raced Filly Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If one of the unexposed OR=120 first-time-out fillies is significantly superior in terms of raw ability and simply outstays or outpaces the field.
scenarios.body: With a large portion of the field either maiden-placed only or wholly unraced, a well-bred newcomer from a powerful yard can overcome a wide-open betting market purely on class; the Joseph O'Brien or Weld yards have strong Naas records and their debutantes must be respected.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sooner than expected and the closers find a clear run through a large, congested field.
scenarios.body: A genuine hold-up horse near the back of the field needs a truly contentious early pace and a gap to materialise in the final furlong — both are unlikely given one front-runner and a compressed midfield of redistributed hold-up types all fishing for the same late run.

watchPoints.text: Acula and Emiza are both unraced three-year-olds from Joseph O'Brien and Dermot Weld respectively — watch for significant market moves at the off, as either yard landing a well-prepared debutante could render the entire pace map secondary.

Nautic Star's odds will reflect whether punters believe she can control this from the front unchallenged — if she drifts markedly it may signal that connections expect a stronger pace than the map suggests, which would fundamentally alter the favoured running style.

Dylan Browne McMonagle's booking for Never The Same (Joseph O'Brien) is a high-profile jockey pairing for a horse with just two runs; watch for market support, as this filly sitting behind a modest pace with a top jockey is the most logical danger to Nautic Star if the closers do get a run.

The large field of 18 on a flat mile at Naas creates a significant traffic risk for all hold-up types — Venosa (Lordan/A P O'Brien) is the most likely to be given the clearest passage by her rider, making her the hold-up horse to monitor if the pace quickens earlier than expected.

Several runners — including Shelton Spring (6 days ago) and Whatsin The Stars (9 days ago) — return on very short turnarounds; if either shows unusual energy in the pre-parade ring it may signal a more forward showing than their debut form implies, which could affect pace in the early stages.
